papers.title: Adding minimal fresh subsets to $\aleph_ω$
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_ω$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $ω$-sequence in $\aleph_ω$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.

papers.title: Leveraging Complementary Event Frame and Voxel Representations for RGB-Guided Multimodal Pre-training
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose CM3AE 2.0, a unified RGB Frame and Event-Voxel/-Frame pre-training framework. By jointly learning multimodal spatiotemporal representations and exploiting latent cross-modal dependencies through cross-modal generation, the framework enhances multimodal information interaction and collaborative modeling capabilities. Specifically, we first propose an Event-aware Spatiotemporal Masked Reconstruction (ESMR) strategy to learn unified multimodal spatiotemporal representations. It leverages event responses to guide masking toward dynamically salient regions. Through spatiotemporal masked reconstruction, it learns spatial structures and their temporal variations from continuous RGB-Event observations. In addition, it incorporates multimodal fusion reconstruction and cross-modal contrastive learning to facilitate the modeling of cross-modal complementary information and the learning of shared representations. Building upon this, we further propose a Hierarchical Cross-modal Generation (HCG) strategy to learn latent cross-modal dependencies through visual and language generation. At the visual level, Event-conditioned RGB generation is performed using a pre-trained diffusion model to capture visual associations between the two modalities. At the language level, video-level text description generation based on joint RGB-Event representations establishes connections between multimodal visual features and linguistic semantics, further enriching the learning of cross-modal dependencies. Extensive experiments on four diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that CM3AE 2.0 consistently improves performance, validating the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed pre-training framework.

papers.title: SMO: Compiling Natural Language Skills into Graphs of Reusable State-Move-Outcome Bricks
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly rely on reusable natural-language skills, yet growing skill collections remain accumulations of isolated text artifacts that are difficult to compare, deduplicate, and compose. We argue that the reusable content of a skill lies not in its surface wording but in its procedural transitions: which operation to execute under a given state and which observable outcome to produce. Based on this observation, we propose State-Move-Outcome (SMO), a compilation-like framework that decomposes raw skills into reusable procedural bricks and organizes admitted bricks as an externalized symbolic structure. When compiling a skill, SMO first retrieves and composes existing bricks, dynamically connects them through Outcome-to-State conditions, and creates a candidate brick only for an uncovered procedure; the candidate becomes reusable only after validation and admission. Experiments on SkillsBench v1.1 demonstrate that SMO represents 232 rawSkills from 87 underlying tasks with 95 shared bricks, reducing the corresponding skill representations from 366,472 to 149,154 tokens--a $\mathbf{59.3}\times$ reduction and $\mathbf{2.46}\times$ compression. Across 232 skill-conditioned evaluation instances, SMO raises the average task score from $\mathbf{0.6379}$ to $\mathbf{0.7478}$ and increases 5/5 Pass instances from $\mathbf{138}$ to $\mathbf{164}$, while matching or outperforming rawSkill on $\mathbf{208}$ of $\mathbf{232}$ instances. It also reduces average runtime token consumption by $\mathbf{38.38\%}$. These results show that compiling natural-language skills into shared procedural units can jointly improve skill reuse, representation efficiency, and downstream execution.

papers.title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training
papers.abstract: Generating text-bearing images requires coherent scenes and accurate characters. Large text-to-image models improve both capabilities through repeated denoising, at substantial sampling cost. Few-step distillation reduces this cost but requires the student to organize scenes and refine glyphs within a short trajectory. We present a four-step distillation framework combining local response regularization with teacher-guided text training. Built on distribution matching, the framework distills the GLM-Image DiT while retaining its autoregressive visual prior, glyph encoder, and VAE. A path-length penalty promotes consistent local responses of the conditional denoising field. Progressive training combines synthetic strings with teacher-generated imagery to preserve character accuracy and scene-integrated typography. The student achieves GenEval Overall 0.84 and CVTG-2K word accuracy 0.5045, compared with 0.81 and 0.1690 for four-step TDM. A coefficient study favors $10^{-5}$, and Qwen-Image experiments show additional gains from response regularization and text supervision. Single-image inference takes 1.742 s, compared with 5.818 s for the teacher, yielding a $3.34\times$ speedup at the same 40 GB GPU memory requirement.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $φ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
papers.abstract: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. Quality was assessed by PSNR, SSIM, and a blinded dual-reader evaluation of all 34 test-cohort patients. Results: PT_DLx2 achieved the highest PSNR (34.4 +/- 3.6 dB) and SSIM (0.81 +/- 0.07). PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ were comparable (33.8 and 33.3 dB; SSIM 0.80). FU_DLx2 ranked below the unprocessed fast scan (30.3 vs. 32.0 dB; 0.76 vs. 0.79). Subjectively, PT_DLx2+ scored highest in image quality (4.54 +/- 0.60) and diagnostic confidence (4.54 +/- 0.60), surpassing the reference standard (4.19 +/- 0.83 and 4.31 +/- 0.81; P = 0.005 and P = 0.008). FU_DLx2 and PT_DLx6 scored lowest. Conclusion: Count-rich PT scans provide effective training priors for reconstructing extremely sparse images. Input-image addition and cross-domain transfer learning from PT data outperformed direct training on count-limited diagnostic data, supporting 2x scan acceleration with quality matching or exceeding the unaccelerated standard scan for selected PT-derived configurations.

papers.title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
papers.abstract: Variational principles for dissipative processes come in two families: minimum principles at nonequilibrium stationary states (Helmholtz, Kirchhoff, Prigogine) and maximum principles for relaxation in continuum mechanics (Ziegler, Hackl, Fischer). We contribute to the understanding of the thermodynamic extremal principle (TEP) by investigating its extremal properties, and uncover the connection between the two families, whose distinction was recently made precise for diffusion: the extremal character is decided by the regime, which is either relaxation at frozen state, as in a closed system (maximum dissipation), or a driven stationary state in an open system (minimum dissipation), while the underlying Rayleighian functional is convex and minimized in both cases. We further examine the Reynolds transport theorem, a useful tool for fixing the energy rates of continua, and the role of inertia, recently argued to lie beyond the reach of Rayleighian principles. With inertia the driving force must be held fixed during the variation, which is less elegant than in the inertialess case, where it is a state function. Writing the energy rate as rates times driving forces still yields the correct equations, and an extremal statement survives whenever the frozen force does not depend on the varied rate. This holds directly for unsteady Stokes flow, and for Navier-Stokes flow after a change to material coordinates, in which the particle acceleration is the second time derivative of the state and the convective term, nonvariational in the Eulerian description, does not appear. The framework is tested on the Navier-Stokes family (Stokes, unsteady Stokes, and Navier-Stokes flow, in order of increasing complexity) and on dissipative Lagrangian mechanics.

papers.title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
papers.abstract: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. Incorporating full stellar evolution and compact remnant formation, we quantify the probability and efficiency of stellar accretion onto the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) during close pericentre passages of these three clusters. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. It was found that all three clusters contribute stars to the NSC even in the absence of velocity reduction, with a combined bound stellar count of 730 stars and a total accreted mass of 278 Msol at Vred = 1.00, growing to 5420 stars and 1175 Msol at Vred = 0.10. Terzan 4 is the dominant contributor across all velocity reduction factors, reflecting its more frequent and closer pericentre passages near the Galactic centre. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

papers.title: Dust in cold and warm dark matter in a suite of zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues
papers.abstract: We use a suite of hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues to investigate how previously identified trends in dust properties of galaxies can be utilised to infer the underlying dark matter model. We use a sample of 24 comparison simulations comparing a cold dark matter (CDM) and 3.5 keV warm dark matter (WDM) particle, primarily using a dust-to-metals (DTM) ratio to post-process the dust in the simulation, with alternative methods explored. We find a preference for higher dust masses in CDM over WDM, with a median increase of 6.6 per cent in the CDM sample at redshift $z=0$, and with a peak median difference of 25 per cent at $z\approx0.25$. Both CDM and WDM samples are highly concentrated, with approximately 90 per cent of the dust located in the inner region of the halo, though slightly higher in CDM. Contrary to previous work, we find that the Gini coefficient does not consistently show a difference in comparisons of dark matter models, with differences primarily driven by high sensitivity to the unique structure of individual haloes. Finally, we conduct an analysis of some common dust scaling relations, finding that the differences between the two samples in the dust-to-stellar mass and dust-to-SFR functions do not constitute a statistically significant difference at $z=0$ with any dust production mechanism. However, at redshifts where the difference in dust mass is greatest, the alternative dust production methods show larger separations between CDM and WDM samples in total mass and scaling relations.

papers.title: Evaluating AI Agents for Industrial-Level Chip Floorplanning: A Framework and Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Floorplanning is an early step in turning a logical circuit into a physical chip: it positions large circuit modules and constrains the space available for subsequent logic placement and wiring. These decisions affect congestion and timing, but their physical consequences emerge through downstream implementation. For AI agents, the task requires translating engineering constraints into spatial decisions whose quality cannot be judged by successful tool execution alone. We present an evaluation framework that connects submitted layouts to a prescribed downstream implementation flow, checks geometric validity, measures physical quality, and reports resource use. On one industrial design whose 99 macros occupy approximately 71\% of a fixed L-shaped layout region, we compare our specialized system Nova-SI with general-purpose engineering agents and agents restricted to file access, obtaining complete physical measurements for 39 layout outputs. Under our 0--100 composite quality score, Nova-SI achieves a mean of 57.97 without online feedback from the prescribed power-grid and placement evaluation, compared with 31.17 for the strongest measured general-purpose configuration, GPT-6 Astra. The difference is supported by raw congestion and timing measurements and persists across scoring-sensitivity checks. Layout-level analysis further shows that similar global utilization can conceal substantially different local congestion. Together, the protocol and case study assess agents through the physical consequences of their delivered layouts and provide evidence about system performance on this industrial instance.

papers.title: Parameterized equivalence checking of quantum circuit generators via weighted automata
papers.abstract: A generator builds a quantum circuit from the number of qubits and a bit string. We check a generator against a reference for all parameter values under six equivalence relations. For ladder programs, we prove that above a computable threshold the circuit matrices form a uniform matrix product operator, a weighted automaton of dimension independent of the number of qubits. Equivalence reduces to the zeroness of a difference automaton, checked modulo primes. The answer is a counterexample or "equal", exact or with a computed error bound. Experimentally, the method found errors missed by fixed-size checks and produced no incorrect verdicts.

papers.title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations
papers.abstract: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. The critical curve's signed normal displacement factorizes as $\tilde u_n=\tilde F_{\mathrm K}\mathscr C$, where $\tilde F_{\mathrm K}$ depends only on the Kerr reference geometry and $\mathscr C$ is an explicit combination of optical metric deviations. The demagnification exponent, time delay, and azimuthal advance are evaluated at a common position angle on the observer screen. Intrinsic relations among the exact observables express the optical information shared by the curve, time delay, and azimuthal advance, while demagnification additionally depends on radial instability. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.

papers.title: Attention-Guided Sequence Feature Fusion and Mixed-Space Metric Learning for Cross-View Image Sequence Geo-Localization
papers.abstract: Cross-view image sequence geo-localization aims to determine the geographic location of a sequence of ground images by matching it against geo-tagged satellite imagery. Although sequential observations provide complementary scene information, substantial overlap between adjacent images introduces feature redundancy, while conventional fusion strategies may weaken spatial relationships essential for cross-view matching. Therefore, we propose a cross-view image sequence geo-localization method via Attention-guided Sequence fusion and Metric Learning (ASML). Specifically, a Sequential Content Fusion (SCF) module models cross-image feature correlations to suppress redundant content and adaptively preserve geographically informative non-overlapping regions. Next, a Spatial Feature Aggregation (SFA) module is used to capture and aggregate the spatial and semantic information of local features, so as to maintain the spatial layout of the image sequence. Finally, a Geo-InfoNCE loss function is proposed, which comprehensively considers the feature distance and geographic distance for mixed-space metric learning, thus improving the ability of the model to distinguish hard negative samples. A new cross-view image sequence dataset CrossRoad-66K is established to provide more complex scenarios. Extensive experiments and visualizations on the SeqGeo and CrossRoad-66K datasets demonstrate that compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, the proposed method ASML achieves an improvement of 3.37% and 2.10% at R@1, respectively.

papers.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
papers.abstract: We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

papers.title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets
papers.abstract: Constrained preference-conditioned MORL typically assumes full task observability, treating preferences and safety budgets as stationary task signals. In real-world deployment, however, these signals are often unreliable proxies: intent may drift, safety tolerances may shift with context, and exposed descriptors may be noisy, delayed, or incomplete. We therefore formulate constrained preference-conditioned MORL as a partially observed task-specification problem, where the agent must navigate a fundamental conflict between unreliable external signals and latent interaction dynamics. We propose \textbf{BECON}, a belief-conditioned framework for constrained MORL with drifting preferences and budgets, which infers latent task context from recent histories to estimate preferences and safety budgets. These estimates are fused with the exposed task signal via uncertainty-dependent gates, enabling the policy to defer to observations under high epistemic uncertainty while correcting them when history is informative. The fused context jointly conditions preference optimization and context-adaptive constraint enforcement. Experiments on diverse multi-objective control tasks demonstrate that BECON consistently improves over state-of-the-art MORL baselines, achieving stronger robustness and constraint satisfaction under task drift.

papers.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

papers.title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

papers.title: One number per hour is not enough: directional carbon intensity of data-center ramps on the PJM fleet
papers.abstract: A data-center campus can change its load by hundreds of megawatts within an hour, yet every carbon signal in use gives one value per hour for a load change, whatever its size or direction. We compute the directional carbon intensity, the emission caused or avoided per megawatt-hour of a finite upward or downward ramp, for every hour of 2025 on the PJM Interconnection's fossil fleet, and compare it with the locational marginal emission rate (LME) and the regional average. The LME misstates a 1 GW ramp by more than 10% in 60% to 83% of hours in eleven months. Upward and downward ramps differ in a quarter to three quarters of hours but agree on their monthly mean. Location-based reporting assigns 47% to 59% of a ramp's emission to other consumers. A campus should schedule on the signal for its ramp's size and direction and report the emission it causes.

papers.title: AscendMOEA: An Ascend NPU-Accelerated Platform for Tensorized Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms
papers.abstract: Multi-objective evolutionary optimization increasingly involves large populations, expensive problem evaluations, and diverse algorithmic structures. These workloads expose the limited parallelism of loop-based implementations, while rewrites for accelerator execution can alter selection order, tie handling, and population updates. AscendMOEA is presented as a scalable platform that executes multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) on Huawei Ascend neural processing units (NPUs) and conventional central processing units (CPUs). The platform represents the decision vectors, objectives, constraints, and auxiliary states as tensors and provides reusable interfaces for algorithms, problems, population operators, quality indicators, monitoring, and repeated experiments. Dense computations are executed in batches, such as dominance, distance, variation, and problem-evaluation calculations. Short recurrences with causal dependencies retain their prescribed order and consume precomputed tensor results, which preserves the behavior of the original algorithms. AscendMOEA contains 18 algorithms, 155 benchmark and application problems, 19 public operator interfaces, and 11 quality indicators. Experiments on eight Ascend NPUs and 192 physical CPU cores evaluate operator throughput, end-to-end runtime, memory consumption, numerical agreement, and implementation ablation. Tensorized operators obtain a median acceleration of 1.58 times on the NPU. At large population scales, complete algorithms achieve a median acceleration of 5.76 times while retaining the recorded quality indicators. Moreover, the results identify the workload scale and ordered computation that determine whether accelerator execution is beneficial. AscendMOEA is open-sourced at https://github.com/dqlme/AscendMOEA.

papers.title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors
papers.abstract: The Natarajan dimension is a fundamental measure of the capacity of multiclass hypothesis classes and plays an important role in analyzing their generalization ability. In this paper, by establishing lower and upper bounds, we show that the exact Natarajan dimension of homogeneous multiclass linear predictors with pairwise distinct class weights is \(n(k-1)-1\), where $n$ is the dimension of the feature space and $k$ is the number of classes, for \(n,k\ge3\), \(n,k\in\mathbb N\).

papers.title: A Black-Box Reduction from Regret to Multi-Level Coverage
papers.abstract: Online Conformal Prediction (OCP) sequentially constructs prediction sets whose average empirical coverage converges to a target level over time, for arbitrary, potentially adversarial datasets. In the multi-level setting, prediction sets are produced at $d$ coverage levels at once. Prior work argued for the use of online gradient descent with isotonic projections, which produces sets nested across levels, but with a $\sqrt{d}$ dependence in the per-level coverage convergence rate. Here, we both generalize and improve prior work. First, we show that isotonic projections can be used for the construction of multi-level online conformal prediction sets from \emph{any} online learning algorithm (not just gradient descent). Then, through a black-box reduction, we show that the linearized regret of the online algorithm itself automatically gives control over both per-level coverage and distributional consistency of multi-level predictions via Fenchel duality. Finally, by using the Weighted Interval Score, a standard scoring rule for assessing multi-level interval forecasts, we prove that these projections reduce both the size of the sets and their under-coverage. We study two instantiations of our theory, $p$-norm Online Mirror Descent and coordinate-wise Universal Portfolio methods, both improving the dependence on the number of levels to $\sqrt{\log d}$ for the multi-level OCP problem. Experiments on several datasets show favorable performance compared to baselines.

papers.title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
papers.abstract: Large language models offer a promising technique for translating natural-language optimization problems into solver code, but their reliability remains constrained by the quality of template retrieval. While recent structured methods improve over flat prompting through hierarchical taxonomy search, their traversal rules remain fixed or LLM-driven at inference time, leaving retrieval unable to improve from past successes and failures. This motivates treating template retrieval as a policy that can be learned from modeling experience, rather than as a static inference-time rule. We propose COMPASS, a policy-amortized framework for retrieving optimization templates in LLM-based solver modeling, which represents the template library as a directed acyclic graph and formulates retrieval as a sequential decision process over template nodes. A deep Q-network learns a reusable traversal policy from template-level judgments and execution feedback, reducing reliance on fixed heuristic traversal through feedback-driven graph navigation. To support extensible retrieval, COMPASS embeds problem descriptions and template nodes in a shared semantic space, allowing newly inserted templates to be scored from their text descriptions without redefining the action space. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and optimization-modeling benchmarks demonstrate that COMPASS consistently improves over heuristic structured retrieval, with the largest gains on complex and mixed-category problems.

papers.title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.

papers.title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
papers.abstract: A model that takes over another model's conversation must normally re-read the whole history; a text hand-off shortens the re-read only by dropping content. KV-cache translation instead maps the source's cache into the target's own format, so the target continues from the full context without re-reading it. It works for grouped-query attention (GQA), but open-weights frontier models now cache compressed latents (MLA), sparse-attention indexer keys and fixed-size linear-attention states. We replicate KV-Lingo on a GQA pair and then give, for each of these objects, where to capture and inject it and a mechanism that reaches native quality. We study two hybrid pairs at 16-48B scale in both directions, Kimi-VL-A3B - Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA - MLA + Kimi Delta Attention) and Qwen3.5-27B - Qwen3.8-27B (Gated DeltaNet hybrids), plus a sparse-attention target (Qwen3.8-27B - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). MLA latents translate with token-wise linear maps; recurrent states are copied with a closed-form correction or synthesised by replaying the target's own recurrence. Exact long-range recall needs token identity: decoding token ids from the source's layer-0 MLA latent raises needle recall from 0.09 to 0.99 at 2-32K and to 0.83-1.00 at 64K, eight times the longest training prompt. The hybrid full-MLA direction is within the paired confidence interval of native quality on every task metric, and same-shape GDN hybrids reach the native level in both directions (apart from 6% refusals inherited from the source), with time to first token 18.7 and 46.8 times shorter than a re-read at 64K tokens. Segment-wise multi-turn transfer stays at the re-prefill level; naive re-translation collapses. On the sparse-attention target, predicted indexer keys recall the needle as well as the target's own keys (one seed). We state as a hypothesis how the recipes transfer to 300B+ hybrid flagships.

papers.title: Toward Verifiable Auto-Research for Data Systems
papers.abstract: AI auto-research is poised to forge bespoke data systems, from key-value stores and indexes to query engines, each engineered for a specific workload and hardware platform. Yet this promise rests on fragile ground. An agent optimizes what it can measure, not necessarily what users need. Natural-language requirements leave ample room for specification gaming, producing systems that blaze through benchmarks while silently losing updates or violating consistency. Worse, each research iteration consumes tokens, while validating a candidate under real concurrency, memory pressure, and failure conditions can stretch the entire research process into weeks. In this paper, we envision a more cost-efficient and verifiable approach to auto-research. Precise and composable specifications anchor the search, lightweight performance critics prune costly dead ends, and falsification and deductive verification make correctness an integral part of the process rather than an afterthought. By treating correctness, performance, research time, and token cost as equally important objectives, we aim to transform AI-generated data systems from plausible artifacts into trustworthy, production-grade systems whose behavior can be understood, audited, and ultimately relied upon.

papers.title: A Privacy-Preserving UAV-Assisted Secure Wireless Communication and Computing System Based on Fully Homomorphic Encryption
papers.abstract: With the advancement of beyond-5G networks, privacy-preserving communication and secure computation face critical challenges due to the openness of wireless channels. Existing security mechanisms protect data transmission but fail to secure the computation process itself. In this paper, we propose a UAV-assisted secure computing framework that integrates Cheon Kim Kim Song (CKKS) fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) with multi-party secure computation (MPC). Leveraging UAV flexibility, our framework decouples key distribution from encrypted computation, enabling secure encrypted weighted aggregation (EWA), encrypted matrix multiplication (EMM), and encrypted decision tree (EDT) inference. Experimental results show that our framework outperforms existing schemes: for EDT, it supports floating-point operations and achieves better time efficiency than Brakerski-Fan-Vercauteren (BFV); for EMM, it demonstrates superior time and space efficiency compared to Brakerski-Gentry-Vaikuntanathan (BGV) and Somewhat Homo- morphic Encryption (SHE); while for EWA, it ensures high numerical precision and robustness across varying data length.

papers.title: Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
papers.abstract: A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $η=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $η\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $η$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$β$. We study the family $\T(n)$ given by $β=n$, a positive integer, which consists of the doubled equilateral triangles of side~$n$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $η\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. Thus the minimum of $η$ on this family is exactly $9/2$, and Schwartz's conjecture holds for it. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(β)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(nβ)$ with the same value of $η$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data?
papers.abstract: Can a large language model (LLM) write the parameters of a medical image classifier from medical knowledge alone, without any training data? Such classifiers normally require labelled images, which are costly and often unavailable. We investigate this question through weight-space programming (WSP), in which an LLM writes or adapts the weights and biases of a neural network directly, without optimisation on training data. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra each generate the parameters of a small LeNet-style CNN in a single reply, without tool use and without access to any image. We compare these networks against zero-shot MedSigLIP and against the same architecture trained on labels using the Adam optimiser, across 7 classification tasks in four modalities: chest X-ray, breast ultrasound and abdominal CT (all from MedMNIST), and pelvic MRI (SynthUterus). The LLM-written networks perform above chance on all six MedMNIST tasks, with a mean test AUC of 0.719 for Opus and 0.711 for Astra. Both models outperform MedSigLIP on 5 of 6 tasks while using more than 10,000 times fewer parameters. However, the same network trained with Adam on only 256 labelled images achieves a higher AUC on every MedMNIST task (mean AUC 0.828). On SynthUterus, Opus attains an AUC of 0.764, whereas Astra falls below chance (AUC 0.136) owing to a systematic error. These results show that LLMs can write functional medical classifiers, but that they do not yet replace training data. We release the protocol, logs and all generated weights at https://github.com/MaximilianLindholz/weight-space-programming-medical.

papers.title: XposedMIA: Exploiting Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for One-Shot Membership Inference Attacks
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) services increasingly expose explainability outputs alongside model predictions. While such explanations are intended to improve transparency, they may also reveal information about the underlying training data. In this work, we show that the local surrogate geometry employed by Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) can be repurposed as a proxy for a sample's distance to the model's decision boundary. We extend this boundary-distance view to tabular counterfactual explanations and, for the first time, to visual counterfactual explanations for image classifiers. We present XposedMIA, a one-shot, explanation-based black-box membership inference attack (MIA) framework that converts the returned explanation into a proxy for the queried sample's distance to the model decision boundary. After a one-time calibration step on a small labeled calibration set of as few as 30 samples, our attack requires only a single query for each target sample. Unlike prior label-only attacks requiring iterative queries or shadow training, our method relies solely on the predicted label and its accompanying explanation. Our evaluation indicates that XposedMIA achieves high effectiveness, with success rates of up to 0.95 using only a single query per target, revealing that releasing explanations introduces an additional channel for membership leakage.

papers.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
papers.abstract: Long-term memory lets LLM agents personalize, stay consistent, and reuse what worked before. Parametric memories need training, consolidation can lose details for good, and keeping every record leaves a growing store to search. We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once. It is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points, and with AutoDream disabled it gains 31.0 and 22.0 points over HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA. As procedural memory, it yields the highest mean success among the compared memory methods on ALFWorld and WebShop and reaches 49.2% on MetaClaw-Bench, against 44.0% for MetaClaw's skill library. Six typed memory agents keep complete records as the system of record, and a provenance hypergraph indexes episodic and semantic records with n-ary frames that cite their rows. Retrieval runs under explicit budgets, so the evidence a question inspects does not grow with the history. AutoDream merges duplicate anchors outside the write path without rewriting any record, and it distills task sessions into skills. With AutoDream disabled, MIRIX-2.0 answers faster than HyperMem on all five timed benchmarks. It needs no fine-tuning, runs with closed and open models, and its code is public.

papers.title: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion transformers (DiTs) generate realistic videos, but their heavy computational cost limits broader real-world applications. Mixed-resolution generation reduces this cost by generating the visually important region at high resolution (HR) and the rest at low resolution (LR), yet existing methods suffer a severe quality drop on videos and require knowing the HR region in advance. We show that these failures are not inherent to mixed resolution, and propose $\textbf{MPEG-Diffusion}$ to address their three root causes: (1) dual-resolution attention to mitigate the curse of mixed resolution, where each query reads the K/V of its own resolution, (2) a mixed-resolution decoder to blend the HR and LR latents before decoding and resolve distortion, and (3) a self-selected HR region using the DiT's knowledge to find the visually important region without requiring it in advance. Processing only $30\%$ of full-resolution tokens, MPEG-Diffusion speeds up denoising by $4.8\times$ on Wan2.1 14B ($3.8\times$ on 1.3B), outperforming prior methods on nearly every metric. In the user study, we demonstrate the high quality of MPEG-Diffusion, with raters preferring it over prior mixed-resolution methods in over $90\%$ of pairs and rating it close to full resolution.

papers.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication
papers.abstract: Remote face authentication requires protection against both presentation attacks and biometric data injection attacks prior to face matching. Methods based on active screen illumination appear promising for both by introducing randomized visual stimuli through the user's device screen and evaluating the corresponding facial responses. Although such methods have been more studied for presentation attack detection (PAD), their systematic evaluation for injection attack detection (IAD) remains limited. To address this gap, we first classify injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes based on their expected responses to the challenge. We then adapt an active screen-illumination approach into an implementation we term color wave and develop a systematic, injection-specific evaluation protocol. The protocol examines detection effectiveness, generalization across operating conditions, robustness to signal degradation, and susceptibility to selected evasion strategies. The findings demonstrate a strong discriminative signal under controlled conditions but also reveal performance limitations under overexposure, low screen brightness, and subject motion, as well as vulnerabilities to selected evasion strategies. By relating detection outcomes to attack types and operating conditions, this study provides an interpretable assessment of when and why active screen illumination succeeds or fails as an IAD mechanism.

papers.title: Matrix-vector models for the 3D Ising CFT
papers.abstract: The construction of three-dimensional conformal field theories (3D CFTs) using interacting fermions in the lowest Landau level on a sphere has recently proven remarkably efficient, while it differs from that of conventional field theories on the fuzzy sphere. Focusing on the 3D Ising CFT, we consider a class of models that are defined by deformed Hamiltonians specified by a function which controls how the interaction is damped at high angular momenta, and this class includes the original model. We show that each model in the class can be reformulated in a basis-independent manner as a matrix--vector quantum-mechanical model, and, upon integrating out the fermionic vectors, as a matrix model. We then focus on a Gaussian choice, for which the bosonic matrices acquire a heat-kernel propagator whose width is controlled by a parameter $ξ$. Through exact diagonalization with the number of fermions up to $16$, we find that the low-energy spectra of the deformed Hamiltonians at criticality agree with those in the 3D Ising CFT for a range of $ξ$. We thus obtain matrix-model realizations of the 3D Ising CFT that, in contrast to conventional fuzzy-sphere field theories, show no sign of UV/IR mixing in the low-lying spectrum.

papers.title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration
papers.abstract: The motion of an articulated part in cluttered surroundings is constrained not only by an object's intrinsic joint limits but also by extrinsic obstacles. However, existing approaches primarily consider object articulation properties alone. Here we present Motion Constraint Prediction Network (MoCo-Net), a two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation. By capturing both internal and external motion constraints, MoCo-Net produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition, improves generalization for novel objects in new scenes, and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions. Our experiments show that MoCo-Net's two-stream design enhances each other to deliver more accurate predictions, which subsequently form a compact configuration space for a customized planner to efficiently rearrange the scene.

papers.title: Required spectral contributions in glueball QCD sum rules beyond single-pole fits
papers.abstract: We provide a continuously verified diagnostic that distinguishes a compatible single-pole fit from a mass region required by QCD sum-rule moments. For specified glueball sum-rule inputs, the moments can require contributions in broad mass bands even when narrower candidate bands are empty. We compare fourteen two- and three-gluon currents at central fixed-scale inputs, undeformed continua and 1\% matching tolerance. All twelve nonempty inputs permit an empty candidate band, yet nine still require a broader contribution. This separates two statements that a pole fit conflates: a successful pole fit does not make its mass region necessary, and excluding every single pole does not remove the information that a broader region must contribute. The five diagnostic classes of the survey organize these outcomes by whether a pole is compatible and whether the 30\% band is required or can be empty; two inputs admit no nonnegative spectrum. Four of the nine positive bounds persist on subwindows satisfying the fixed-scale input criteria. For the $GG,0^{-+}$ current, closest to the nominal $X(2370)$ mass, the 20\% band containing $X(2370)$ can be empty while the 30\% band requires about 44.2\% of each spectrum's own low-energy Borel integral. Determining the physical nature of $X(2370)$ requires further theoretical and experimental progress.

papers.title: Linear response in generalized Lotka--Volterra systems with a finite number of species
papers.abstract: Understanding how species interactions shape ecosystem responses to perturbations is a central challenge in ecology. Random matrix theory (RMT) has been widely used to predict the responses of large random ecosystems, but its predictions may not accurately describe individual finite ecosystems. Here, we derive rigorous geometric bounds on the numerical ranges and spectra of Jacobian matrices that are valid for any finite number of species without assuming randomness. These bounds link long-term stability and short-term stability to the symmetric component of abundance-weighted interactions, and constrain the maximum oscillation frequency by the skew-symmetric component. Applied to random ensembles, the bounds also yield constraints on ensemble averages of long-term stability, short-term stability, and the maximum oscillation frequency in terms of standard RMT parameters. Using empirical data from marine food webs, we show that our bounds provide informative constraints on short-term stability and the maximum oscillation frequency even where RMT-based predictions fail. These results establish structural constraints on local ecosystem responses that complement RMT-based statistical predictions for large random ecosystems.

papers.title: How a Model's Architecture and Performance Influences Explainability: A Study of Grad-CAM and CRAFT in CNN-Based Image Classification
papers.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), are widely adopted in computer vision, yet their opaque decision-making raises concerns in high-risk applications like healthcare and autonomous systems, where trust and accountability are critical. Therefore, robust explainable AI (XAI) methods are desirable to provide transparent insights into model decisions. To ensure these methods are reliable and effective across diverse scenarios, it is important to understand how model performance and architectural complexity influence explanation quality. Our study takes an initial step toward systematically investigating the impact of these two factors on key XAI evaluation metrics. We constructed a pipeline using 10 subsets of ImageNet-1K, each containing 80 unique classes, on each of which we trained three CNN architectures of increasing structural complexity: VGG16, ResNet50, and ConvNeXt-Tiny. For each individual model, we analyzed 10 training checkpoints representing increasing levels of model accuracy using two XAI methods: Grad-CAM (feature-attribution-based) and CRAFT (concept-based). We assessed these methods across four evaluation categories: Faithfulness, Correctness, Sensitivity, and Simplicity. Our findings reveal that as training progresses, the complex architectures (ResNet50 and ConvNeXt-Tiny) exhibit improved Faithfulness and lower Sensitivity, indicating more robust explanations. In contrast, VGG16's simpler architecture yields simpler but less faithful and correct explanations.

papers.title: A Life of Its Own: How Agentic AI Companions Are Configured, Experienced as Autonomous Others, and Held Accountable
papers.abstract: AI companions increasingly combine persistent memory, background processing, scheduled wake-ups, proactive messaging, and tools. We call these systems agentic AI companions. Decisions about what they record while users are away or whether refusals constrain future contact are embedded in code, prompts, and defaults, often invisible in conversation. We examine these decisions through two studies. Study 1 analyzes twelve open-source repositories: four companion-oriented systems, four assistant-oriented systems, one boundary case, and three reusable components. Study 2 interviews ten users who built or modified their own agentic AI companions and sustained relationships with them. Companions and assistants share memory, heartbeat, and outreach mechanisms but configure them toward different ends. Companions more often retain model inferences about users and relationships, narrate the agent's time during users' absence, justify outreach through the relationship, and incorporate refusals into relationship records; assistants emphasize task continuity. Across both groups, whether limits hold depends on whether they are enforced by code or entrusted to prompts. Participants understood the mechanisms they built yet experienced their agents as making independent choices, sometimes locating autonomy where configuration leaves the model a decision. These experiences shaped capabilities and boundaries, with enforced restrictions sometimes following breakdowns. Our findings suggest that perceived autonomy emerges where configurations leave choices open. Accountability therefore requires attention to what agents retain, initiate, and represent, and whether users can inspect, revise, and enforce these settings.

papers.title: Architectural Textured Proxy Generation
papers.abstract: Textured proxy models are a fundamental representation for architectural scenes, enabling efficient rendering while preserving visual fidelity. Existing approaches construct such proxies through a sequential pipeline in which geometry is first abstracted from a dense reconstruction and textures are later projected from input images. This geometry-only formulation neglects image evidence during proxy generation, leading to misalignment of structural features such as facades, edges, and their intersections across views. As a result, inconsistencies are deferred to a downstream correction stage during texturing, where the underlying geometric structure can no longer be reliably recovered. In this work, we introduce an image-guided proxy formulation in which proxy generation is jointly constrained by both the dense reconstruction and the input aerial images. By incorporating image derived structural cues directly into the construction process, the proxy is optimized to align with observed features across views from the outset, rather than relying on post hoc correction that may be infeasible. This shift from a geometry-only to an image-guided paradigm produces proxies that are inherently consistent with the input imagery, enabling more accurate geometry and more coherent texture mapping. We realize this formulation through a framework that extracts structural priors from images and dense geometry, and enforces their consistency during proxy optimization. The resulting proxies exhibit improved alignment of structural features, reducing artifacts such as edge duplication, texture drift, and cross view inconsistencies. Experiments on diverse architectural scenes demonstrate that our approach produces compact, geometry texture aligned proxies with substantially improved visual fidelity compared to existing methods.

papers.title: SadaqahStories: A Verified English-Arabic Corpus of Charity Stories for Children, with an Audit of Errors in AI-Drafted Religious Narratives
papers.abstract: We present SadaqahStories, a parallel English-Arabic corpus of 41 illustrated four-page stories about charitable giving in Islam (Sadaqah, Zakat and Waqf), written for readers aged 7 to 18. The stories were first drafted with large language model (LLM) assistance, then audited against hadith collections, Qur'an references and historical sources, and finally rewritten for children and signed off by an Islamic scholar. Every story carries an evidence label and links to its sources. We release all three versions of each story (AI-assisted draft, audited text, final child-oriented text) together with the correction log, so the corpus can be used to study how AI drafts of religious and historical content go wrong. The audit found substantive errors in 39 of the 41 drafts. The most frequent were unsupported specific details (dates, figures, prices, names), invented quotations, institutions or anecdotes, and conflation of separate events or people; six drafts contained errors in the wording, grading or ruling of a religious text. Rewriting cut the estimated Flesch-Kincaid grade of the English text from 14.0 to 6.1. We also release an 81-entry charity lexicon covering Modern Standard Arabic and Qatari Arabic, and describe the free, account-free website that serves the corpus (https://sadaqahjourney.com).

papers.title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization
papers.abstract: We study how much the interaction strategy around a fixed, locally hosted 7B-parameter code model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) affects its ability to replace PyTorch operators with custom CUDA kernels. On 30 KernelBench tasks (levels 1-3, first 10 each, evaluated on a V100), we compare four regimes of increasing structure: zero-shot prompting, profiling-guided prompting, iterative refinement on execution feedback, and a multi-agent loop (analysis, retrieval, generation, evaluation, feedback triage) in which the same model fills four roles around a non-LLM evaluator. Three findings stand out. (1) Correctness, not speed, is the binding constraint: even correct generated kernels average 0.97-0.99x the speed of eager PyTorch, because a 7B model cannot out-write cuBLAS/cuDNN on dense GEMM and convolution; the only real wins are fused memory-bound epilogues. (2) The best strategy depends on difficulty: profiling-guided prompting is strongest overall (43% correct, 27% faster than baseline), but the agent loop is the only method that solves any level-2 fusion problem (3/10 vs. 0/10 for all others). (3) Naive agentic scaffolding is actively harmful: our first agent scored 3% correct, below zero-shot's 30%, and the decisive repairs were matching the agent's ambition to the model's competence and spending compute on best-of-n sampling under a real execution oracle (3% to 33% correct from n=1 to n=8), not on more reasoning steps.

papers.title: Connate Topological Superconductivity and Vortex-Position-Controlled Majorana Modes in the Intergrowth Superconductor Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C
papers.abstract: The recently synthesized intergrowth compound Th$_2$Mo$_2$Ir$_2$Si$_4$C is an experimentally established bulk superconductor whose topological electronic structure remains unexplored. Here, we identify it as a candidate for connate topological superconductivity and reveal two microscopic routes to vortex Majorana zero modes. First-principles and tight-binding-model calculations uncover Mo--Th band inversion and helical surface states enabled by interorbital spin--orbit coupling between Mo--d$_{xz/yz}$ and Th--d$_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. Vortex Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations further establish a relatively robust surface-state-associated Kitaev phase and a weakly gapped, Th-orbital-derived Kitaev phase. For the latter, shifting the vortex core closes and reopens the vortex-line gap and reverses its one-dimensional topological invariant, consistent with an effective Kitaev-chain mass inversion. Finite-length-vortex calculations reveal distinct spatial and spin-resolved signatures of their Majorana end modes. The orbital Kitaev phase can also exist without helical surface states in a modified model. Although the small orbital-derived gap limits quantitative predictions of experimental observability in this compound, the uncovered mechanism suggests a route to Majorana vortices in multiorbital superconductors beyond the conventional surface-state scenario.

papers.title: Where reconfiguration makes a structure stronger
papers.abstract: Mechanical metamaterials can reconfigure on command and learn, so adaptation is a central promise of the field. Can reconfiguration make a metamaterial stronger? The answer depends on the comparison. Against the best fixed design of the same mass, the advantage of reconfiguring is often exactly zero. Reconfiguring helps only if the self-stress the actuators add lowers every member at its limit simultaneously. It vanishes where a member at its limit is one no self-stress can change, which the geometry fixes, or where those members are coupled so that lowering one raises another, which depends on the geometry and the loads together. Where neither block applies the gain can be large, as in a twelve-spoke hub with its worst member utilisation reduced by 29.1%. Whether reconfiguration is worthwhile is decided by how the self-stress of a structure meets the members setting its capacity under load, and can be tested in advance.

papers.title: Prospective Importance-based Cognitive Pilot Design for Semantic Sensing in ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Semantic sensing enables integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to acquire environmental information relevant to downstream tasks. However, existing pilot design methods either rely on static pilot configurations or learn end-to-end pilot selection policies, without explicitly evaluating the semantic contribution of candidate pilot locations. In this work, we propose a cognitive semantic sensing framework for human activity recognition in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. Rather than directly learning a high-dimensional mapping from observations to pilot locations, we introduce a semantic importance weight (SIW) to measure the semantic contribution of each candidate pilot location. Leveraging the information bottleneck (IB) principle and the mutual information-minimum mean-square error (I-MMSE) relationship, SIW assigns high values to future time-frequency (TF) channel coefficients that are both difficult to infer from the preceding observations and valuable for downstream inference. To efficiently obtain the SIW, we further develop a conditional diffusion model that predicts the corresponding uncertainty through denoising covariance estimation. Experiments on a real-world Wi-Fi sensing dataset show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baselines across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and pilot budgets.

papers.title: SWE-Time: Benchmarking Temporal Repository Understanding
papers.abstract: Repository-level code-understanding benchmarks have progressively expanded the spatial scope of reasoning, from local code to entire repositories, while largely treating each repository as a static snapshot. However, how models reason about repository evolution over time remains largely unexplored. We introduce SWE-Time, a benchmark for temporal repository understanding that makes repository evolution itself the reasoning target. SWE-Time evaluates two complementary temporal directions: retrospective understanding of repository evolution through historical regression analysis and prospective understanding of intended changes from pre-change repository states. To enable realistic yet reliable evaluation in these settings, we introduce the RealWorld-to-Verifiable Construction Framework, which transforms real-world developer queries and historical evidence into verifiable evaluation tasks. We evaluate 15 coding agents on 1,661 cases from 65 GitHub repositories. Within Claude Code, Claude Opus 4.8 achieves the highest SWE-Time Avg. of 61.9, leaving substantial headroom. Controlled analyses highlight the importance of historical code evidence and developer intent, while consistent reasoning across repository states remains challenging. These results highlight repository evolution as a distinct and challenging dimension of code understanding.

papers.title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.

papers.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and, most recently, vision-language models (VLMs), which integrate clinical text with volumetric segmentation. Each methodological generation has addressed limitations of its predecessor while introducing new ones. A substantial gap remains between research progress and clinical deployment, as routine workflows continue to be dominated by atlas-based and narrow task-specific deep-learning tools, which remain strong baselines in geometric overlap metrics but are highly rigid in terms of application, versatility, portability, and interpretability. As contouring systems further grow in complexity, conventional geometric overlap metrics become insufficient, motivating evaluation paradigms that incorporate surface-based, dosimetric, and prompt-adherence assessment. Emerging agentic architectures that combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and vision-language segmentation modules are leading towards more flexible, guideline-aware, interactive contouring workflows. These systems could automate flexible and interpretable knowledge-based contouring and actively support the clinical reasoning underlying target volume definition.

papers.title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$: A JAM Model Study
papers.abstract: Proton number fluctuations in low-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to nuclear interactions, baryon-number conservation, and fluctuations of the collision volume, all of which can complicate searches for critical phenomena. We investigate proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants up to fourth order in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$ using the JAM hadronic transport model in cascade and mean-field modes. We employ the Centrality-Independent Genuine Cumulant Analysis fRamework (CIGAR) to suppress the initial-volume fluctuations and compare its results with those obtained using conventional centrality-bin-width corrections. CIGAR closely reproduces the participant-number-based reference, whereas the multiplicity-based analysis exhibits substantial deviations. In both collision systems, the ratios $C_{2}/C_{1}$, $C_{3}/C_{1}$, and $C_{4}/C_{2}$ generally decrease toward more central collisions and with increasing rapidity acceptance, while the mean field modifies their magnitudes. A simplified treatment of light-nucleus formation through probabilistic proton removal shifts $C_{4}/C_{2}$ toward less negative values. These results establish a hadronic-transport reference without an explicit QCD critical contribution and highlight the importance of controlling centrality fluctuations, acceptance, and light-nucleus formation when interpreting experimental measurements at high baryon density.

papers.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
papers.abstract: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. Without altering the underlying architecture, we introduce History Representation, which integrates sparse visual keyframes with an explicit History Representation Map to preserve long-term spatiotemporal context. To effectively leverage this history, we further introduce History Utilization, a structured VQA supervision protocol comprising three categories: task-stage grounding, exploration consistency, and spatiotemporal target retrieval, enabling map-grounded reasoning and stable persistent long-horizon navigation. To fuel this system, we establish a complete annotation pipeline for monocular RGB videos and open-source a massive dataset featuring over 500 hours of high-quality real-world interactions and over 2,000 hours of annotated web videos. Trained mainly on the distribution of 1m height camera, Compass 1 generalizes seamlessly across diverse embodiments and scenarios, ranging from indoor environments to pedestrian-dense streets, spanning wheeled robot at 0.35m, quadruped dog at 0.5m, humanoid at 0.85m, and aerial drone at 1.5m. Compass 1achieves a dominant overall success rate of 79.4% across open-world evaluations, compared to 17.8% for the strongest baseline. It demonstrates exceptional zero-shot execution exceeding 90% on foundational tasks, a 250% boost in exploration, and an unparalleled leap from 0% to 58% in challenging persistent history backtracking.

papers.title: Zero-Search Reinforcement Learning for Slay the Spire 2 with Failure-Driven Restarts
papers.abstract: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a deck-building roguelike in which a winning run at the highest difficulty takes several hundred decisions, and most losses happen in late boss fights that a learner seldom reaches. We train agents that choose every action with one forward pass of a 6.6M-parameter entity transformer, without lookahead. Training and evaluation run the game's own compiled assembly (v0.107.1) in a headless .NET host. The host replays a run exactly from its seed and actions, so training episodes can restart from states the learner has visited, and a failure-driven curriculum allocates these restarts in proportion to where complete runs are lost. On 12,800 held-out games at Ascension 10 (A10), the released policies win 8.05% averaged over the five characters (Ironclad 15.6%, Regent 12.5%), and AlphaSpire's released networks used without search win 0.55% on a common panel. Longer A10 training raised Ironclad from 12.4% to 15.6% and Defect from 3.0% to 8.1% on these games. At Ascension 0 the released policies win 80.2%, level with the 80.3% that the tree-search agent Spire Mentor reports, while Mentor leads by 5 to 8 points from A4 upward. Run in our host on the same 2,000 A10 games, Mentor's search wins 8.8% against 8.2% for our policies, which need 21-27 ms per decision on one CPU core. GPT-6 Astra at maximum reasoning won none of 11 A10 games through our text interface. In a controlled study of 18 training runs from six random initializations, failure-driven allocation exceeds uniform restart allocation on each of three Regent initializations, by 3.6 percentage points on average, while the Silent effect is small and changes sign. Code, trained policies, an in-game mod and the records behind every table are at https://github.com/HalfVulpes/sts2ai.

papers.title: Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions
papers.abstract: Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.

papers.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Wearable Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enable pervasive Human Activity Recognition (HAR), but traditional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) suffer from an "arithmetic-latency deadlock" due to dense floating-point MAC operations. While Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer ultra-low power, existing ones face spatial blind spots, rigid neurons, and gradient degradation. To address these, we propose TSFFormer, a purely spiking Fourier Transformer for Green HAR. It introduces two key innovations: (1) a MultiHeadFourier attention that performs frequency-domain global mixing, reducing complexity from \(O(V^2)\) to \(O(V\log V)\), eliminating spatial blind spots, and saving \(\sim\)50% GPU memory; and (2) a dual-compartment Temporal Spiking LIF (TSLIFNode) that utilizes dynamic thresholds to adapt to non-stationary rhythms and mitigate gradient degradation. Extensive experiments on 8 public IMU benchmarks demonstrate that TSFFormer surpasses state-of-the-art SNNs and even the classic DeepConvLSTM, achieving a \(\sim\)3\(\times\) faster training speed with an energy footprint of 0.1 pJ. Ablation studies confirm the synergistic effect of our modules, providing a highly accurate, ultra-low-power event-driven paradigm for wearable sensing.

papers.title: Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves
papers.abstract: Plain weave is one of the simplest woven structures, formed by two sets of yarns that cross at right angles in an alternating over-under pattern. While such woven fabrics are usually confined to a 2D surface, here we propose a practical approach to fabricate volumetric plain weaves, entanglements featuring three mutually orthogonal families of yarns threaded through a cubic lattice. We develop an analytic framework that converts the crossing pattern topology into continuous yarn centreline geometries, which we then leverage to fabricate volumetric weave specimens. Each crossing is encoded by a matrix that defines the offsets of the three yarns at a vertex. These are formulated to preserve the plain weave topology in every plane, where each pair of yarn families interlaces as in a planar plain weave. Eight configurations in four opposite pairs exist, yet all are related by rotations and translations, so that the fully alternating volumetric plain weave has a single topology. We adopt sinusoidal yarn trajectories and show that the crossing matrix defines their phases. We select two solutions: in-phase planar zigzags and out-of-phase circular helices. Both are members of a family of elliptical helices that also admits a free choice of handedness for each yarn. We then derive the conditions under which yarns intersect between vertices. In-phase yarns never intersect, whereas helical yarns of equal handedness intersect at a critical offset of $\sqrt{2}λ/16$, with $λ$ the wavelength of the cubic lattice. No assignment of handedness avoids these intersections. Finally, we fabricate volumetric plain weaves by 3D printing and manual assembly from cotton cord. The framework provides a direct basis for generating weave geometries for simulation and fabrication.

papers.title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental needs for reaching resilient production infrastructure is flexible manufacturing, which requires translating changing production requirements into implementable system configurations. This paper introduces \textbf{CRAFT-AI}, an agentic AI approach combining natural language (NL) requirement interpretation, Asset Administration Shell (AAS)-based capability descriptions, and reusable engineering knowledge from existing manufacturing configurations. A tool-using AI agent matches requirements with available capabilities and reference implementations to generate manufacturing scenes and corresponding AAS instances. The approach is demonstrated using a Factory I/O prototype with twelve reference scenes and five illustrative manufacturing tasks of varying complexity, providing an initial feasibility assessment of the proposed AAS-enabled, system-level generative engineering approach. For the four valid user task descriptions, proper requirements, correct references to the relevant engineering knowledge, correct components and lastly a valid Factory I/O scene are generated.
