Production-cost models provide chronological commitment and dispatch, but stability analysis requires corresponding electrical detail and device dynamics. This paper introduces KPG193-ext, an extension of the synthetic Korean power-grid test system KPG193 that links chronological operating points with detailed electrical and dynamic models. The extension adds synchronous-machine, controller and renewable-converter models, together with explicit voltage levels, generation terminals, inter-voltage and step-up transformers, and reactive compensation. The resulting 731-bus network retains the original 193 regional locations. Daily unit commitment followed by hourly AC optimal power flow establishes 8,760 operating points for 2025, each distributed as paired steady-state and dynamic-model files. Selected-hour studies examine generation-loss frequency response, steady-state flow-voltage characteristics, and rotor-angle response with special protection system actions. The results reveal differences in delivered frequency support, internal voltage stress along regional transfer paths, and the angle-frequency tradeoff of corrective generator tripping. The database provides a common basis for examining the stability implications of commitment, dispatch and corrective action across daily and seasonal operating conditions.

papers.title: Exploring public-private data sharing practices through the lens of Open Data Ecosystems: A multiple case study on municipal and regional freight logistics
papers.abstract: Background: Freight transport is expected to increase, contributing to air pollution. There is, therefore, a critical need for increased efficiency that can reduce emissions. Data sharing is one approach, where actors within Open Data Ecosystems (ODE) collaborate and share data among stakeholders to plan and operate more efficient and sustainable freight transport. Aim: In this study, we explore how public-private data sharing practices in municipal and regional last-mile freight logistics in Sweden may improve efficiency. Method: Following a prolonged participation process, we conducted a multiple-case study involving three different cases, built upon initial meetings, semi-structured interviews, supported by a thematic analysis, and validated through a follow-up workshop. Results: The findings show that data sharing in public-private freight logistics (ODE-PPF) is shaped by interrelated socio-technical aspects, including platform design, roles of actors, handling of sensitive data, data quality, and procurement processes. We synthesize our findings in an actor model and a conceptual model, highlighting how these aspects contribute to the functioning of ODE-PPF, and derive seven proposition sketches as a foundation for future research. Conclusion: Data sharing is a central mechanism enabling integration and value creation in last-mile logistics. It depends on the interaction between technical and organizational aspects. Public actors can undertake a key role as a neutral keystone actor by orchestrating the ecosystem and facilitating data sharing through governance practices such as procurement.

papers.title: Deriving Tsallis Entropy from First Principles
papers.abstract: The kinetic approach for q-distribution is extended through a "bottom-up" procedure to the corresponding entropic formula. In this way, the validity of Tsallis' formula, S_q(W) = k_B ln_q(W), is established from first principles. The resulting q-entropy is additive and the zeroth law of thermodynamics is automatically satisfied because the conventional identification beta = 1/(k_B T) remains valid. Entropy, energy, and all relevant quantities for both discrete and continuous cases are evaluated using standard (linear) averages. The "bottom-up" and "top-down" approaches yield the same q-distribution for velocities. The standard results are naturally recovered in the limit q -> 1.

papers.title: When Handshakes Go Dark: An Adaptive Semantic-Sequential Fusion Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is essential for network security monitoring and traffic management. Self-supervised pre-training can learn reusable representations from large-scale unlabeled traffic, but TLS 1.3, QUIC, and privacy mechanisms such as Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) increasingly conceal application, handshake, and service-identifying information. Observable upper-layer bytes are therefore dominated by ciphertext, weakening the link between raw-byte patterns and application semantics and limiting model generalization. Moreover, the availability and discriminative value of observable information vary across protocols, protection profiles, and tasks, complicating classification across diverse scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose FLARE, a Field-aware Learning and Adaptive Representation Fusion framework for encrypted traffic classification. FLARE pre-trains a BERT-based packet encoder through Masked Field Prediction, which reconstructs masked tokens from field-structured context. During downstream fine-tuning, the parameters of the pre-trained packet encoder remain frozen, and a packet-level gated module adaptively combines protocol-semantic representations with directional packet-length representations. A flow-level encoder then models inter-packet dependencies for classification. We evaluate FLARE on eight datasets spanning diverse encrypted-traffic tasks, including CipherSpectrum and VisQUIC for strongly encrypted scenarios. FLARE achieves superior performance over baselines across the eight datasets, exceeding the strongest pre-trained baseline by 10.92 percentage points on QUIC website fingerprinting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of field-aware pre-training and adaptive semantic-sequential fusion under constrained observability.

papers.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
papers.abstract: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE

papers.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

papers.title: LongSCOP: Semantically Consistent Long Video Outpainting
papers.abstract: Video out-painting is an important problem, yet existing research focuses primarily on short clips, leaving long video out-painting largely underexplored. Extending video out-painting to long videos poses substantial challenges. A natural solution is iterative out-painting, i.e., generating videos chunk by chunk, but this introduces two major issues: generation instability or even failure caused by inter-chunk inconsistencies and error accumulation, and semantic drift over long temporal horizons. In this paper, we propose LongSCOP, short for Semantically Consistent long Video Out-Painting. First, we introduce a training recipe with three components for smooth and stable long-horizon generation: self-forcing training, latent calibration, and future references. Beyond generation stability, we recognize that the rich temporal context of long videos provides valuable references for maintaining semantic consistency. We therefore develop a VLM-based agent that automatically selects the most informative reference frames from the entire video to maintain consistent subjects, scenes, and backgrounds throughout long-horizon generation. We also construct a high-quality training dataset of 62K video clips. To facilitate research on this underexplored problem, we introduce LVO-Bench, a benchmark curated by human experts to assess long-horizon stability and semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in both generation stability and semantic coherence.

papers.title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
papers.abstract: Symbolic knowledge (motif counts, ring counts, label constraints) is routinely added to graph neural networks (GNNs) and justified by their limited expressivity. We replace this yardstick with an exact one. The largest log-loss reduction a rule $S$ can give a model family is $I(Y;S\midσ)$ given what the family computes; every realised gain splits exactly into this term plus repaid neural debt; and for a trained network with representation $T$ the value is $I(Y;S\mid T)$, the label information training failed to extract. Rule design thus becomes rule discovery: we score candidates on the network's out-of-fold residual against calibrated permutation nulls with family-wise error control. On ZINC, discovery recovers the hidden ring term $\max(0,\ell_{\max}-6)$ of the target in three independent runs ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}=0.001$) and beats expert cycle counts; frozen and applied to five unseen datasets it is never significantly worse than the plain network or the expert rule, and on BBBP it significantly beats both.

papers.title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
papers.abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

papers.title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
papers.abstract: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from $3000$ to $20000$ $\mathring{A}$), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra $C$ and $A$ caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope $1/p$ and size $r_{s}$, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form $r_{s}$ $\propto$ $λ^{p}$. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with $p=4/3$. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are $r_{s}=4.9^{+2.3}_{-2.6}$ $\sqrt{M/0.3M_{\odot}}$ (lt-day) and $p=0.77^{+0.47}_{-0.28}$, respectively, reinforcing a departure from the standard accretion disk model ($ T \propto r_s^{-3/4}$).

papers.title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
papers.abstract: We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\inΩ\subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(Ω; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality \[ |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } Ω \] with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(Ω)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $Ω$.

papers.title: $λ_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
papers.abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

papers.title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $Θ_{e_\ell}Θ_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.

papers.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
papers.abstract: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

papers.title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
papers.abstract: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $σ(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $σ(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.

papers.title: Real Topology on Symmetry-Invariant Loops Enforces Superconducting Pairing Zeros
papers.abstract: Normal-state topology can obstruct superconducting pairing and give rise to gapless nodes in the quasiparticle spectrum. However, existing pairing-obstruction mechanisms largely rely on Fermi-surface topology or global Bloch-band topology. Here, we establish a new and general mechanism: one-dimensional (1D) real topology, defined on antiunitary-symmetry-invariant loops, enforces pairing zeros without requiring Fermi-surface or global Bloch-band topology. We derive sufficient conditions and lower bounds for pairing zeros across diverse pairing channels, for both zero and finite Cooper-pair momenta. The theorems apply to systems of arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the pairing bands to be globally isolated. We further show that such topologically enforced pairing zeros, if isolated, necessarily carry odd vorticity and can give rise to Bogoliubov-de Gennes nodes and zero-energy boundary modes, as demonstrated in a minimal two-orbital model. Our results reshape the understanding of how normal-state topology can obstruct the superconducting order, highlight the significant role of 1D real topology beyond single-particle band phenomena, and provide a general framework for identifying candidate materials hosting nodal superconductivity.

papers.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

papers.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
papers.abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

papers.title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
papers.abstract: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.

papers.title: Causal discovery from Bayesian symbolic regression
papers.abstract: Causal discovery from observational data is central to scientific reasoning, yet established constraint-based and score-based methods often recover only a Markov equivalence class and provide no signal in bivariate or strongly autocorrelated regimes typical in some areas of science. Here, we recast causal discovery as a Bayesian symbolic regression problem. Given a set of candidate parents for each target variable, the Bayesian symbolic regression samples closed-form expressions from a posterior over symbolic models. The fraction of sampled expressions in which each candidate variable appears defines a posterior inclusion probability that we use as the causal score. This replaces pointwise model selection by an ensemble of plausible mechanisms. We evaluate the method on coupled nonlinear bivariate dynamics, on the CauseMe benchmark suite spanning linear, chaotic, nonlinear, higher-dimensional and high-noise settings, and on a four-variable biogeoscience structural causal model under Gaussian, heavy-tailed and mixed-noise regimes. Our approach is competitive with, and often outperforms, specialized causal discovery algorithms. Additionally, the method returns closed-form mechanisms leading to explicit causality and interpretability.

papers.title: Fiscal Commitment and the Additionality of Philanthropy: Heterogeneous Donor Purposes in a Shared Public Budget
papers.abstract: Philanthropic donors often value different public services, while a budget authority allocates public spending across a shared portfolio. Policy frameworks frequently seek to ensure that private finance supplements rather than displaces public funding. We distinguish baseline additionality, which preserves pre-gift public funding, from portfolio preservation, which preserves a service's provision after all gifts are pooled under discretionary budgeting. A larger gift to one service raises the discretionary provision of every service and reduces the protection slack available to the others. This cross-donor fiscal externality yields an exact feasibility result: if a service's maximum permissible floor lies below its discretionary post-gift provision, every effective protection reform reduces that service relative to the portfolio reference, including full protection of its own appropriation. Conversely, a reform that expands at least one donor-backed service while preserving all others exists exactly when every maximum floor reaches the reference. The paper characterizes the complete preservation set and its welfare-maximizing element. Under logarithmic preferences, donation shares determine protectability, while heterogeneous donor valuations determine welfare incidence. Baseline additionality may therefore hold while a service loses fiscal benefits generated by other gifts.

papers.title: Revealing laser-induced modification of weak ferromagnetism through a spin-reorientation phase transition in iron borate Fe$_3$BO$_6$
papers.abstract: In the iron oxide Fe$_3$BO$_6$ weak ferromagnetism stems from competing contributions from two-site Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) and from on-site anisotropies at the two $4c$ and $8d$ types of nonequivalent Fe$^{3+}$ sites. As a result, spin reorientation (SR) transition $Γ_2$ $\rightarrow$ $Γ_4$ in Fe$_3$BO$_6$ uniquely comprises 90$^\circ$ spin switching and a 35% change of weak ferromagnetic moment. We explore ultrafast kinetics of such a transition as a proxy for weak ferromagnetism contributions modified by femtosecond laser pulses. Using magneto-optical pump-probe technique we reveal that the SR transition is triggered by an abrupt decrease of the weak ferromagnetic moment in the $Γ_2$ phase, and relate it to the laser-induced modification of the DMI and anisotropy contributions to the spin canting. By tuning the pump pulse phonon energy between different optical absorption ranges, we show that laser-driven impact on spin canting possesses a nonthermal character and is achieved through the charge-transfer transitions $2p\rightarrow3d$ within Fe$^{3+}$O$^{2-}_6$ octahedra rather than by localized $3d\rightarrow3d$ transitions at Fe$^{3+}$. The decreased weak ferromagnetic moment controls the threshold and the latency of the SR transition, as well as a final state. The latter is achieved via the precessional switching to the $Γ_4$ phase activated by the laser-induced heating. Final state is found to be a coexistence of $Γ_4$ and $Γ_2$ phase with modified spin canting persisting even at hundreds of picoseconds.

papers.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
papers.abstract: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

papers.title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
papers.abstract: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

papers.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

papers.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
papers.abstract: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. BPE's pretokenizer splits on whitespace before merges are learned, so no multi-word string can ever become a single token: in Qwen3-4B, "United States of America" is four tokens and no adjacent pair of them exists as one entry, so a phrase is out of reach of any method drafting in the target's vocabulary. We change the unit. A small MLP head reads the frozen target's hidden state and predicts a one- to three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary; greedy longest-match expansion maps it back into the target's own tokens, and N candidates are verified in one forward pass behind a prefix-tree mask, so the change is orthogonal to tree depth and width. The target and its tokenizer stay frozen and a candidate is accepted only while it matches the target's own argmax, so the served output is identical to greedy decoding up to floating-point tie-breaking. On one A5000 at batch 1, against HuggingFace generate(), a 21.94M head (0.545% of Qwen3-4B) reaches 2.391x on GSM8K, 2.444x on MATH-500 and 1.544x on MT-Bench. Because the head's output layer is one row of 257 parameters per entry, the draft vocabulary size is the parameter budget: an 8,000-entry head is 3.434M parameters, 0.0854% of the target and 64x smaller than EAGLE-3's drafter, and keeps 92.3% of the larger head's GSM8K tokens per pass. With EAGLE-3 run on same prompts and baseline, our 21.94M head is ahead of tree-16 on both maths sets and behind tree-60 on every set.

papers.title: Giant Diffusion at Flocking Transitions
papers.abstract: We simulate dynamics in two-dimensional aligning active-matter models exhibiting order-disorder transitions in the velocity field. Analysis reveals that the single-particle diffusivity, $D_s$, exhibits strong enhancements at criticality which we quantify via a finite-size scaling method. This dynamical behavior at nonequilibrium flocking transitions is fundamentally different from that at the criticality of equilibrium systems, where diffusivities either vanish or remain non-critical. Furthermore, $D_s$ exhibits pronounced finite-size effects throughout the ordered phase, which also are absent in equilibrium settings. We interpret these counterintuitive transport anomalies within the framework of a flocking theory. Our results suggest that enhanced diffusion generates effective long-range interactions. This relaxes the constraints of the Mermin-Wagner theorem that otherwise prevents order-disorder transitions in two dimensions for systems possessing continuous symmetry. These results are of much experimental relevance and have important implications in formulating quantitative theories for nonequilibrium transports.

papers.title: Prediction with Foundation Models under Deployment Budgets
papers.abstract: Foundation models can supply predictions for a downstream task that draw on knowledge from extensive pretraining, but they differ in task-specific accuracy and query cost. We develop a framework that improves prediction for the task under a budget on the average query cost per input, using training data to learn which models to query and how to combine their outputs with features available without querying. The first method queries the same models for every input; the second lets them vary across inputs and uses Q-learning to decide which model to query next and when to stop. For the first method, we show that several individually inaccurate outputs can jointly outperform the best single one. It attains the minimax rate when the regression function depends on the outputs only through models within the budget. Otherwise, any method within the budget can be forced to a slower rate, which the first method attains. For the second method, we show when varying the queried models across inputs strictly improves on querying the same models for every input, and bound its prediction risk and average cost in finite samples. In simulations and a multimodal laptop price application, both methods outperform existing methods.

papers.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
papers.abstract: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =κ\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $κ$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

papers.title: Sets of reach $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}\left( 1/R^2\right)$
papers.abstract: Positive reach underpins many results in computational geometry and topology. It is used for triangulation criteria, topological inference, and manifold learning. The geometric properties of these sets have therefore been studied intensely. In this paper we focus on the intrinsic metric properties of sets of positive reach. In particular we give an elementary proof of the fact that (closed) sets of reach at least $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$. This fact was established earlier by Alexander and Bishop, using quite significant machinery. The fact that a space is $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$ offers many advantages, such as the uniqueness and continuity of sufficiently short geodesics, the existence of Fr{é}chet means and by extension the Rips based homotopy reconstruction of Hausmann is available.

papers.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
papers.abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.

papers.title: The Connection between Halo Assembly History and the Stellar Distribution II: A Radially Stratified Fossil Record of Past Halo Mass
papers.abstract: The spatial stellar distribution in massive central galaxies preserves a stratified fossil record of their host halos' assembly history. Using a halo-mass-complete sample from the IllustrisTNG-300 hydrodynamical simulation at $z=0.4$, we quantify this connection with two diagnostics. The fossil correlation $\tildeρ(z)$ measures how strongly a present-day galaxy property retains information about the progenitor halo mass at each redshift. The rank retention fraction $f_{\rm ret}(z)$ measures how many halos selected by that property today were among the most massive halos at each epoch. The central stellar mass at different galactocentric radii exhibits non-monotonic fossil correlations with past halo mass, peaking at intermediate redshifts that systematically shift from $z\sim1$ in the inner regions to $z\sim0.7$ in the outer stellar halos. These peak redshifts are robust from group to cluster scales. Partial correlations with halo accretion rate show that each peak marks the end of the epoch when that component's buildup was sensitive to halo accretion. The rank retention fraction shows that the annular stellar masses of the central galaxy beyond 10 kpc are less biased tracers of the most massive halos at intermediate redshifts than richness. This stratified fossil record originates mainly from the ex-situ phase of galaxy assembly. The outer stellar halo also traces the satellite population at intermediate redshift better than present-day richness. These results establish that the stellar profile of massive central galaxies encodes a radially stratified fossil record of halo assembly history.

papers.title: Attainable and unattainable quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $θ_\ast=Ω/(Ω+ω)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.

papers.title: ADZE 2.0: rarefaction estimates of allelic richness and private allelic richness for whole-genome
papers.abstract: Allelic richness and private allelic richness describe how alleles are distributed across populations, but both depend strongly on sample size. Rarefaction makes them comparable by computing the expected number of alleles in subsamples of a common size, and ADZE implemented this approach and an extension to alleles shared only by a set of populations. However, ADZE was developed for microsatellite data and cannot read sequencing data in variant call format (VCF). Here we present ADZE 2.0, which reads VCF, computes each statistic genome-wide or in genomic windows, and can treat blocks of phased SNPs as haplotype alleles. We also implement improved memory handling and multi-threading support. ADZE 2.0 reproduces the ADZE 1.0 estimates for human microsatellite data exactly. On chromosome 22 of the high-coverage 1000 Genomes Project data, private allelic richness for all 325 population pairs took 4.4 minutes on 32 threads. ADZE 2.0 is available at https://github.com/szpiech/ADZE.

papers.title: The full length of short pants
papers.abstract: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Optimised Distillation for Nucleon Correlation Functions
papers.abstract: The calculation and analysis of nucleon correlation functions is essential for understanding the observed spectra and structure of these ubiquitous hadrons. Two challenges arise in their analysis: at early Euclidean times, they are dominated by excited state contributions and at later Euclidean times, the signal-to-noise ratio degrades exponentially. This leads to a common challenge in identifying a reasonable window on which to extract the ground state energy. By modulating the contribution of each Laplacian eigenmode to the correlator via distillation profiles, we build optimised operators which improve the overlap with the nucleon ground state. In these proceedings, we present our progress on constructing optimised distillation profiles for nucleons and their excited state suppression in two- and three-point correlation functions.

papers.title: Learning to Select Sparse Linear Solvers with Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We investigate convolutional-neural-network (CNN) based automatic solver selection for sparse linear systems, a problem of practical importance where solver performance varies dramatically with matrix sparsity structure. A CNN is trained to regress log timing ratios between candidate solvers using spy plot images of matrix nonzero structure as input, achieving strong prediction accuracy on both held-out SuiteSparse matrices and real-world matrices from high-performance simulation codes.

papers.title: Scalable operating currents in amorphous W-N/FePt superconducting rectifiers
papers.abstract: We demonstrate high-efficiency, field-free superconducting diode behavior in W-N/FePt bilayers fabricated entirely by sputtering at room temperature. The devices combine amorphous W-N superconducting thin films with a 48-nm-thick FePt layer exhibiting remanent stripe-domain magnetization. We used lithographically patterned microbridges to compare W-N/FePt bilayers with single-layer W-N reference films at three nominal W-N thicknesses (18, 24, and 28 nm). The bilayers exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of approximately 4.1-4.3 K. At zero applied magnetic field, the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics exhibit pronounced nonreciprocity, controlled by the orientation of the in-plane remanent FePt magnetization relative to the transport current. The diode response is maximized for perpendicular alignment, reverses polarity upon magnetization reversal, and is strongly suppressed when the magnetization is aligned with the current. This behavior is consistent with asymmetric vortex entry and motion governed by the magnetic stray fields generated near the bridge edges. At 3 K with the remanent magnetization perpendicular to the current, increasing the W-N thickness from 18 to 28 nm widens the current interval between the dissipation thresholds for opposite polarities from about 0.3 to 1.55 mA. All three bilayers exhibit diode efficiencies of approximately 75-80% in this configuration.

papers.title: Perturb, Aggregate then Reconstruct: Consensus Aggregation and Fourier-Attended Multi-Decoders for Reconstruction-based Multi-View Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Multi-view anomaly detection is crucial for industrial inspection to identify defects hidden from single viewpoints. Yet, despite their strong success in single-view applications, reconstruction-based methods remain largely underexplored in multi-view settings. A key challenge in extending these methods lies in generating view-consistent pseudo-anomalies. To address this, we propose PAR, a reconstruction-based framework for enhanced multi-view anomaly detection. First, we introduce a feature perturbation strategy coupled with a consensus aggregation module that integrates these perturbed features across viewpoints to mitigate view-inconsistent anomalies and construct highly aligned pseudo-anomaly representations. Second, we employ a view-specialized multi-decoder architecture; by assigning a dedicated decoder to each view, we increase the model's representational complexity, enabling the generation of highly feasible, localized anomaly maps rather than less precise, view-agnostic reconstructions. Last, we incorporate Fourier attention into the decoders to emphasize global frequency-domain structures over local token evidence, effectively preventing identity mapping. Extensive experiments on the Real-IAD dataset demonstrate that PAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in sample-level, image-level, and pixel-level anomaly detection. Our code is available at https://github.com/SpatialAILab/PAR_mvad.

papers.title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions
papers.abstract: Answer accuracy alone does not distinguish failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application. AuDiR (Audio Diagnostic Reasoning) examines these distinctions through controlled input interventions. Each item contains an audio clip, a multiple-choice question, a task-general rule, and a textual description of the acoustic observations needed to answer. Three conditions progressively supply the rule and observations; a fourth removes the audio while retaining the question and rule. The first correct diagnostic condition assigns an operational response label, without identifying a unique internal cause. The current benchmark contains 201 items in 18 families drawn from 9 sources, with answer references documented separately from percept extraction. In a preliminary evaluation of Gemini-3.8-flash, accuracy is 29.3% without supplied information, 31.3% with the rule, and 98.5% with the observations also supplied. No-audio accuracy is 23.9%, with a confidence interval containing the 25.0% chance rate. A family-level knowledge probe associates incomplete rule recall with larger gains from rule provision. These results show the benefit of supplying acoustic observations as text, while incomplete validation, possible recognition shortcuts, and non-monotonic responses limit stronger failure-attribution claims.

papers.title: Brief introduction to post-quantum cryptography in industrial applications
papers.abstract: The development of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is directly motivated by the necessity to secure information in the face of the quantum threat. This paper provides an overview of recent developments relevant to PQC adoption across several industrial applications, including IoT, healthcare, civil and infrastructure engineering, and defense. We present a brief, self-contained overview of PQC and its market positioning. We perform implementation experiments on selected quantum-safe methods and quantify several aspects, such as the quantum resources required to break common cryptographic schemes, as well as the performance of the most well-known PQC algorithms. We also discuss the resistance of different PQC classes to quantum attacks and the status of PQC implementations in different programming languages. Finally, we present benchmark results on KEMs and signature algorithms to help select the appropriate algorithm for a specific application based on criteria such as algorithm performance, data lifetime, and level of data sensitivity.

papers.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
papers.abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $α$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/λ)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/ε^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.

papers.title: Universal two-qubit control across dilution refrigerators via a 10-km coherent optical link
papers.abstract: Distributed quantum networks are important for scalable quantum processors and for potential applications in communication, distributed computation, and sensing, in which direct classical links for adaptive control are essential to harness the shared entanglement. However, controlling superconducting quantum processors from a separate refrigerator over long distances remains elusive. Here, we introduce a coherent optical link (COL) that delivers microwave waveforms and their phase references between dilution refrigerators. Combining a laser, a microwave-to-optical transducer and an optical-to-microwave photodiode, the COL transmits microwave control signals over 10~km of fiber, while optical references derived from the same laser compensate for the frequency mismatch between devices. Through the COL, we deliver a universal gate set to a transmon qubit and a cavity qubit in another refrigerator and entangle them, and achieve a Bell-state fidelity of 80.6\%. Quantum control delivered through the COL thus provides a classical backbone for modular quantum processors.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

papers.title: Schottky barrier height modulation and memristive behavior in a mechanically exfoliated $MoS_2$ flake with multiple lateral electrodes
papers.abstract: Van de Waals materials possess great potential as core active materials for novel electronics, optoelectronics, and sensing applications. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and other low-dimensional materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and binary oxides exhibit memristive behavior, making them attractive candidates as building blocks for resistive memories and neuromorphic computing devices. In this work, we investigate two-terminal lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few layer $MoS_2$ flakes. We study the influence of the Schottky barrier height (SBH) as a function of the contact area. We report different SBHs from 60 meV up to 208 meV in the same $MoS_2$ flake and analyze the effect of the SBH in the memristive-like $J-V_{DS}$ curves and the observed non-volatile/volatile resistance switching. Our results highlight the importance of contact engineering to obtain different memristive properties in $MoS_2$-based devices.

papers.title: Resetting-based designated information distribution
papers.abstract: For a network of $n$ nodes under random gossip dynamics, we show that by introducing the additional resetting mechanism (with rate $β$) to a designated subset of $r$ nodes, the expected sum of all node values is asymptotically equal to $\tfrac{n}{r}$ times the sum of the initial values of the $r$ designated nodes, in the small-$β$ and long-time limit. We also analyze the convergence speed to this asymptotic state and provide an approximate high-probability confidence interval for the expected sum at finite time $t$ and finite $β$. Operationally, we propose a protocol that distributes the initial node values over the designated subset evenly (up to a prescribed precision), by appropriately turning on and off the resetting dynamics. Our work not only offers insights into classical problems such as distributed computing and network control, but also serves as a potential foundation for designing quantum algorithms that prepare desired states in quantum networks using only local operations.

papers.title: Optimizing the Steady-State Travel Time of Nash Flows over Time with Capacity Increases
papers.abstract: We study budgeted capacity augmentation for single-source single-sink \NFOTs under constant inflow $u_0$. The goal is to increase capacities on arcs subject to a global budget constraint in order to minimize the steady-state travel time in the network. We show that this problem is weakly NP-hard on series-parallel networks and provide an exact pseudopolynomial algorithm as well as a fully polynomial algorithm that attains the optimum travel time for budget $B$ while spending at most $B + \varepsilon\cdot\max\{B,u_0\}$. On general networks the problem becomes strongly NP-hard. Moreover, unless $\text{P} = \text{NP}$, for every fixed $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, no polynomial-time algorithm can achieve the optimal steady-state travel time while exceeding the budget by at most a factor of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$. Lastly, we give structural properties about steady-state travel time under varying arc capacities. We identify capacity thresholds determined by subsets of $s$-$t$-cuts and show that the travel time is constant in the interior of the cells resulting from the corresponding hyperplane arrangement.

papers.title: Detecting AI-Authored Text in Authentic Student Writing: Evidence from PISA 2025
papers.abstract: AI-text detectors reach near-perfect scores in evaluations that contrast fully human-written texts with texts generated from researcher-designed prompts. In authentic student writing, however, AI use is voluntary and often partial. We study this setting with the PISA 2025 FLA dataset, in which 15-year-olds in Germany wrote English argumentative essays with and without access to a gpt-4o-mini-based chatbot. Keystroke, clipboard and chat logs let us trace every character of the final essay to its origin. From this provenance, we derive text- and sentence-level labels for human-written, AI-generated and mixed text, and for text written after chatbot use without traceable AI material. We evaluate a feature-based detector and a classifier on frozen Llama-3.1-8B embeddings, both adapted from top-ranked shared-task systems. Both separate AI from human text reliably (macro-F1 up to 0.96 for texts and 0.95 for sentences), independently of spelling errors. The feature-based detector, however, relies on lexical complexity, which a simple student-style rewriting prompt removes (AI recall 0.92 $\to$ 0.60 with gpt-4o-mini, 0.41 with Qwen3). The embedding-based detector stays robust for whole texts (AI recall $\geq$ 0.94) but not for single sentences (AI recall as low as 0.59). Mixed text falls between the two classes, and text without traceable AI material is classified as human-written in about 95\% of texts.

papers.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
papers.abstract: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

papers.title: Gravity Without Absolutes
papers.abstract: By formulating his theory of universal gravitation in absolute space and time, Newton demonstrated the power of reductionism; it has been behind every major advance in physics since then. However, the lack of significant advances over the last half-century, together with unresolved problems in the dominant paradigms of physics and cosmology, suggest that holism may need to replace reductionism as the way forward. The ontological simplicity and historical significance of Newtonian gravity makes it the ideal theory for examining this possibility. Taking Newton's second law of motion to be the core of his theory, we show that its use within the reductionist framework of absolute space and time introduces an infinity of arbitrary solutions if used to describe $N$-body universes rather than subsystems within them. We show that Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason (PSR) eliminates the infinite arbitrariness and transforms the predicted nature of $N$-body universes; they are all shown to be unexpectedly interesting. An even greater change is enforced if one asks what principle could determine the number of particles in the universe. The PSR suggests it can only be infinite. We suggest that, in such a universe, correlation could replace causation while still giving the appearance that each state has been created by dynamical evolution from the past, whereas its actual explanation may lie entirely within the present state. While much work remains to develop these ideas into a viable theory, we are confident that it advances the case for holism.

papers.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
papers.abstract: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $β=(β_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_β$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_iβ_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $β_i$ on each block. Here $n_β$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.

papers.title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

papers.title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant. The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

papers.title: Textraction: Unified Text-Guided Speaker Extraction and Enhancement for Single- and Multi-Channel Audio
papers.abstract: We present Textraction, a text-guided speaker extraction framework that enables the selective extraction of desired speakers or noise sources from an audio mixture using only natural-language descriptions. The proposed method operates within a single unified model that supports both single-channel and multi-channel inputs and it allows conditioning on either semantic textual descriptions of the target source or on its spatial description. Dedicated single- and multi-channel encoders feed a shared stack of time--frequency transformer blocks, which is conditioned on the prompt and on the recording configuration in every block through cross-attention and estimates the target directly from the mixture in one forward pass, without a separation stage or a source-selection stage. The system can extract an arbitrary subset of entities from a mixture, assuming up to two simultaneously active speakers and two noise sources, and interprets prompts specifying which entities to keep, which to remove, or both. In addition, we show that the framework naturally applies to a speech-enhancement setting, in which a single target speaker is present alongside background noise. To circumvent the application of computationally costly large language models used in prior work, we introduce a lightweight, task-adapted text encoder obtained by contrastively fine-tuning a compact text-retrieval model, which learns to be sensitive to instruction polarity (e.g., keep vs. remove) while remaining robust to paraphrasing. Experiments across attribute-based extraction, spatially guided extraction, and speech enhancement show that the proposed approach effectively isolates the desired entities under various acoustic and spatial conditions, and matches or surpasses dedicated spatial-extraction and enhancement baselines while offering substantially greater flexibility.

papers.title: An Alternative to Quantum Theory
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable empirical success of quantum theory, the interpretation of measurement and the nature of entanglement correlations remain open questions. We outline an alternative framework that seeks to recover the empirical results of quantum theory from a holistic, scale-invariant ontology. Assuming only point particles in Euclidean space, characterised by ratios of masses (and charges) and by the ratios of their mutual separations, the theory describes shapes through a single scale-invariant function; no dynamical evolution is required. In principle, this framework provides a unified description of finite subsystems embedded in a configuration of infinitely many particles and offers a possible route to deriving the observed structures of atoms, molecules and macroscopic bodies without invoking standard quantum mechanics.

papers.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
papers.abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.

papers.title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.

papers.title: Quantitative stability of classical, entropic, and doubly entropic Wasserstein barycenters
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show how the recent analysis of (sharp) strong convexity properties of the Kantorovich functional by the third author can be used to establish new global quantitative stability estimates for Wasserstein barycenters and their entropic regularizations with respect to perturbations of the population distribution. For classical Wasserstein barycenters, we improve the state-of-the-art Hölder continuity exponent with respect to the $\mathcal{W}_1$ metric from $1/6$ to $1/4$, while drastically weakening the assumptions on the population distribution. We also provide an example which shows that the exponent $1/4$ cannot be improved. Motivated by computational considerations, we also analyze regularizations of Wasserstein barycenters with \emph{outer} and \emph{inner} entropic penalizations. For outer entropic barycenters, we establish novel higher-order stability results and in particular give a quantitative bound on relative Fisher information. Another contribution of our paper is a strong convexity estimate for an entropic version of the Kantorovich functional via soft Legendre transforms, enabling us to extend our stability results to \emph{doubly} entropic barycenters, as introduced by Chizat.

papers.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
papers.abstract: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.

papers.title: Dynamic Topological Completeness for $\mathbb R^2$
papers.abstract: Dynamic topological logic (${\bf DTL}$) combines topological and temporal modalities to express asymptotic properties of dynamic systems on topological spaces. A dynamic topological model is a triple $\left <X,f,V\right >$, where $X$ is a topological space, $f:X\to X$ a continuous function and $V$ a truth valuation assigning subsets of $X$ to propositional variables. Valid formulas are those that are true in every model, independently of $X$ or $f$. A natural problem that arises is to identify the logics obtained on familiar spaces, such as $\mathbb R^n$. Slavnov showed that any satisfiable formula could be satisfied in some $\mathbb R^n$ for $n$ large enough, but the question of how the logic varies with $n$ remained open. In this paper we prove that any fragment of ${\bf DTL}$ that is complete for locally finite Kripke frames is complete for $\mathbb R^2$. This includes ${\bf DTL}^\bigcirc$; it also includes some larger fragments, such as ${\bf DTL_1}$, where ``henceforth" may not appear in the scope of a topological operator. We show that satisfiability of any formula of our language in a locally finite Kripke frame implies satisfiability in $\mathbb R^2$ by constructing continuous, open maps from the plane into arbitrary locally finite Kripke frames, which give us a type of bisimulation. We also show that the results cannot be extended to arbitrary formulas of ${\bf DTL}$ by exhibiting a formula which is valid in $\mathbb R^2$ but not in arbitrary topological spaces.

papers.title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
papers.abstract: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.

papers.title: Text Grouping Changes Completion-Time Comparisons in Long-Form Simultaneous Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Does grouping translation updates before speech synthesis change the measured completion gap between two translators? We compare StreamAtt with its fixed-audio-history baseline on ten English-German talks. For each translation, we keep the intended text and its availability times fixed and vary how updates are grouped for synthesis. Four-second grouping increases StreamAtt's mean completion lead from 106.6 to 229.1 seconds with XTTS-v2, but reduces it from 169.5 to 146.5 seconds with Piper. Both produce shorter audio; different changes in playback idle account for the opposite effects. These directions recur on a separately selected twenty-talk panel.
